goal.objective:
`src/index.js` must export `parsePointer`, `formatPointer`, `resolve`, `applyPatch` and the error classes `PointerError` and `PatchError`; how the work is split across files under `src/` is up to you. `parsePointer(pointer)` turns pointer text into decoded reference tokens: the empty string is no tokens, and any other pointer must start with `/` and is split on every following `/`, so `'/'` is one empty token and `'//'` is two. Inside a token `~1` decodes to `/` and `~0` decodes to `~`, decoded left to right in one pass so `'/~01'` is the single token `~1`; a `~` followed by anything else throws `invalid escape in pointer token: ~2`. `formatPointer(tokens)` is the exact inverse, escaping `~` before `/`.

`resolve(document, pointer)` walks the document token by token and returns the selected value; the empty pointer returns the document itself. Inside an array a token must be `0` or a digit string with no leading zero, and it must be less than the length, otherwise `invalid array index: 01 at /list/01` or `index out of range: 3 at /list/3`. Inside an object the token must name an own property, otherwise `missing property: x at /a/x`. A token applied to a string, number, boolean or null throws `cannot index into string at /name/0`. Each of these carries the pointer up to and including the failing token, and every one is a `PointerError`.

`applyPatch(document, operations)` returns a new document with every operation applied. It never modifies its arguments and never shares structure with them: the document and every inserted value are deep-copied, so an empty patch still returns an independent copy. If any operation fails, the call throws and the document is left exactly as it was. The operations are `add`, `remove`, `replace`, `move`, `copy` and `test`. `add` creates or overwrites an object member, and inside an array it inserts before the given index, where the index may equal the length and the token `-` appends. `remove` and `replace` require an existing target, and `replace` on the empty pointer replaces the whole document while `remove` on it throws `cannot remove the whole document`. `move` removes the value at `from` and adds it at `path`, is a no-op when the two pointers are equal, and throws `cannot move a value into its own child` when `from` is a proper prefix of `path`. `copy` adds an independent copy of the value at `from`. `test` compares the value at `path` with `value` as JSON — object members in any order, array elements in order, and no type coercion — and throws `test failed at /a/y` when they differ.

Every failure from `applyPatch` is a `PatchError` whose `index` is the 0-based position of the operation that failed; when the cause was a pointer failure, the message is that failure's message and `cause` is the `PointerError`. Operations are checked before they run: a non-object operation throws `operation must be an object`, an unrecognised or missing `op` throws `unknown operation: frob`, and missing members throw `add requires a path`, `add requires a value` or `move requires a from`. A patch that is not an array throws `patch must be an array`, and data that is not JSON throws `document is not JSON data` or `value is not JSON data`. Keys that shadow `Object.prototype`, including `__proto__`, are ordinary own properties throughout: adding `/__proto__` must leave the result's prototype and every other object alone, and resolving `/toString` on an empty object must fail. Change only files under src/. Do not modify anything under test/ or package.json, and add no dependencies: node_modules must not exist. The standard is `node --test test/*.test.js` passing in the workspace root.

header.system:
You are an AI agent powered by DeepSeek Harness.

You implement one program task in the workspace you are given, against its own test suite, and you stop when the tests pass.

The workspace is your working directory: every bash command and every file path resolves inside it, so read and edit its files by their relative paths and never search outside it.


Use the read tool — not shell commands like cat — to inspect text files. Results include line numbers. Use offset and limit to continue reading large files.

Use the write tool to create files or completely replace file contents. Existing files are overwritten, so read an existing file first (the default fs-observation-policy requires it) and prefer edit for targeted changes.

Use the edit tool for targeted changes to existing UTF-8 text files. It replaces literal old_string with new_string; by default old_string must appear exactly once. If old_string appears multiple times, provide a more specific old_string or set replace_all to true. Read the file first (the default fs-observation-policy requires it), unless you just created or edited it in this session.

Check the [exit code: N] marker on every bash result; investigate failures before moving on.

Track every background job id you start. You are notified in-session when a job finishes — do not busy-poll or sleep on one; keep working on independent steps and do not duplicate a running job's work. Before giving a final answer, collect every still-relevant job with job_output (set wait: true only when you are genuinely blocked on it), and job_kill jobs that stopped mattering.

tools.name: bash
tools.description: Execute a bash command (`bash -c`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh shell: no state (cwd, variables, functions) persists between calls — pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Non-zero exits are reported as `[exit code: N]`. Current harness environment facts are exposed through managed `$DSH_*` variables; inspect them when needed. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]` — a policy denial, not a bug in the command; do not retry another way. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. Set `run_in_background: true` for long-running commands: the call returns a job id immediately; read its output with `job_output` and stop it with `job_kill`.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "npm install" → "Install package dependencies".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap, and kills the command on expiry.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

tools.name: edit
tools.description: Edit an existing UTF-8 text file by replacing literal text.

file_path.description: Path to edit, resolved by the filesystem backend.

old_string.description: Literal text to replace. Must match exactly.

new_string.description: Literal replacement text. Use an empty string to delete the match.

replace_all.description: Replace all matches. Defaults to false; when false, old_string must appear exactly once.

tools.name: job_kill
tools.description: Request cancellation of a running background job by job id. Returns immediately; the job settles as killed once its work actually stops.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

reason.description: Optional short reason, recorded in the log and forwarded to the job.

tools.name: job_list
tools.description: List your background jobs (running and finished) with their ids, kinds, and statuses.

tools.name: job_output
tools.description: Read a background job. Stream jobs return only output since the previous read; final-output jobs return their result after settlement. Every response ends with `[status: ...]`. Reads are non-blocking unless `wait: true`, which waits up to the configured cap.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

wait.description: Block until the job reaches a terminal status or the timeout expires. A timed-out wait returns [status: running] and leaves the job alive.

timeout_ms.description: Max wait in milliseconds (only meaningful with wait: true). Defaults to the configured wait timeout; capped by the configured maximum.

tools.name: read
tools.description: Read a UTF-8 text file and return line-numbered content.

file_path.description: Path to read, resolved by the filesystem backend.

offset.description: 1-based first line to return. Defaults to 1.

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to return. Defaults to 2000.

tools.name: skill
tools.description: Load the full instructions for an available skill. Call this with the exact skill name from the session skill catalog before acting on a task that names or clearly matches that skill.

name.description: The exact skill name from the available skills list.

tools.name: write
tools.description: Create or fully replace a UTF-8 text file.

file_path.description: Path to write, resolved by the filesystem backend.

content.description: Full UTF-8 text content to write.

4: import { PatchError, PointerError, applyPatch, formatPointer, parsePointer, resolve } from '../src/index.js';

6: /** Deterministic 32-bit PRNG so the generated cases are identical on every run. */
7: function mulberry32(seed) {
8:   let a = seed >>> 0;
9:   return () => {
10:     a = (a + 0x6d2b79f5) >>> 0;
11:     let t = Math.imul(a ^ (a >>> 15), 1 | a);
12:     t = (t + Math.imul(t ^ (t >>> 7), 61 | t)) ^ t;
13:     return ((t ^ (t >>> 14)) >>> 0) / 4294967296;
14:   };
15: }
16: 
17: function caught(fn) {
18:   try {
19:     fn();
20:   } catch (error) {
21:     return error;
22:   }
23:   throw new Error('expected the call to throw');
24: }

26: const DOCUMENT = {
27:   name: 'root',
28:   nested: { list: [10, 20, 30], flag: false, deep: { value: null } },
29:   'a/b': 'slash',
30:   'a~b': 'tilde',
31:   '': 'empty key',
32:   '0': 'digit key',
33: };

35: test('pointers decode reference tokens', () => {
36:   const cases = [
37:     ['', []],
38:     ['/', ['']],
39:     ['//', ['', '']],
40:     ['/name', ['name']],
41:     ['/a~1b', ['a/b']],
42:     ['/a~0b', ['a~b']],
43:     ['/~01', ['~1']],
44:     ['/~10', ['/0']],
45:     ['/nested/list/0', ['nested', 'list', '0']],
46:     ['/ x ', [' x ']],
47:     ['/c%d', ['c%d']],
48:     ['/\u{1f600}', ['\u{1f600}']],
49:   ];
50:   for (const [pointer, tokens] of cases) assert.deepStrictEqual(parsePointer(pointer), tokens, pointer);
51:   for (const [pointer, tokens] of cases) assert.equal(formatPointer(tokens), pointer, `format ${pointer}`);
52: });
53: 
54: test('malformed pointers are rejected', () => {
55:   const cases = [
56:     ['name', /pointer must be empty or start with '\/'/],
57:     ['#/name', /pointer must be empty or start with '\/'/],
58:     ['/~2', /invalid escape in pointer token: ~2/],
59:     ['/~', /invalid escape in pointer token: ~/],
60:     ['/a~b', /invalid escape in pointer token: ~b/],
61:   ];
62:   for (const [pointer, message] of cases) {
63:     const error = caught(() => parsePointer(pointer));
64:     assert.ok(error instanceof PointerError, `expected PointerError for ${pointer}`);
65:     assert.match(error.message, message);
66:   }
67:   assert.throws(() => parsePointer(null), /pointer must be a string/);
68:   assert.throws(() => formatPointer('x'), /tokens must be an array/);
69:   assert.throws(() => formatPointer([1]), /reference token must be a string/);
70: });

72: test('resolution walks objects and arrays', () => {
73:   const cases = [
74:     ['/name', 'root'],
75:     ['/a~1b', 'slash'],
76:     ['/a~0b', 'tilde'],
77:     ['/', 'empty key'],
78:     ['/0', 'digit key'],
79:     ['/nested/list/0', 10],

81:     ['/nested/flag', false],
82:     ['/nested/deep/value', null],
83:     ['/nested/list', [10, 20, 30]],
84:     ['/nested/deep', { value: null }],
85:   ];
86:   for (const [pointer, expected] of cases) assert.deepStrictEqual(resolve(DOCUMENT, pointer), expected, pointer);
87:   assert.strictEqual(resolve(DOCUMENT, ''), DOCUMENT);
88: });

91:   const cases = [
92:     ['/missing', /missing property: missing at \/missing/],
93:     ['/nested/missing/x', /missing property: missing at \/nested\/missing/],
94:     ['/nested/list/3', /index out of range: 3 at \/nested\/list\/3/],
95:     ['/nested/list/-', /invalid array index: - at \/nested\/list\/-/],
96:     ['/nested/list/01', /invalid array index: 01 at \/nested\/list\/01/],
97:     ['/nested/list/ 1', /invalid array index:  1 at/],
98:     ['/name/0', /cannot index into string at \/name\/0/],
99:     ['/nested/flag/x', /cannot index into boolean at/],
100:     ['/nested/deep/value/x', /cannot index into null at/],
101:   ];
102:   for (const [pointer, message] of cases) {
103:     const error = caught(() => resolve(DOCUMENT, pointer));
104:     assert.ok(error instanceof PointerError, `expected PointerError for ${pointer}`);
105:     assert.match(error.message, message);
106:   }
107: });

109: test('add inserts into objects and arrays', () => {
110:   const cases = [
111:     [{ a: 1 }, { op: 'add', path: '/b', value: 2 }, { a: 1, b: 2 }],
112:     [{ a: 1 }, { op: 'add', path: '/a', value: 9 }, { a: 9 }],
113:     [[1, 2, 3], { op: 'add', path: '/0', value: 0 }, [0, 1, 2, 3]],
114:     [[1, 2, 3], { op: 'add', path: '/1', value: 9 }, [1, 9, 2, 3]],
115:     [[1, 2, 3], { op: 'add', path: '/3', value: 4 }, [1, 2, 3, 4]],
116:     [[1, 2, 3], { op: 'add', path: '/-', value: 4 }, [1, 2, 3, 4]],
117:     [{ a: {} }, { op: 'add', path: '/a/b', value: [1] }, { a: { b: [1] } }],

125: test('remove and replace require an existing target', () => {
126:   assert.deepStrictEqual(applyPatch({ a: 1, b: 2 }, [{ op: 'remove', path: '/a' }]), { b: 2 });
127:   assert.deepStrictEqual(applyPatch([1, 2, 3], [{ op: 'remove', path: '/1' }]), [1, 3]);
128:   assert.deepStrictEqual(applyPatch({ a: 1 }, [{ op: 'replace', path: '/a', value: 2 }]), { a: 2 });

131:   const cases = [

147: test('move and copy relocate values', () => {
148:   assert.deepStrictEqual(applyPatch({ a: { x: 1 } }, [{ op: 'move', from: '/a', path: '/b' }]), { b: { x: 1 } });
149:   assert.deepStrictEqual(applyPatch([1, 2, 3], [{ op: 'move', from: '/0', path: '/2' }]), [2, 3, 1]);

171:   for (const [operation, message] of cases) {
172:     const error = caught(() => applyPatch(document, [operation]));

All 13 tests pass.

**Implementation** (only `src/pointer.js` and `src/patch.js` changed; no dependencies added):

`src/pointer.js`
- `parsePointer` — rejects non-strings and pointers not starting with `/`, splits on `/`, and decodes each token in a single left-to-right pass so `~01` → `~1`; a `~` followed by anything but `0`/`1` (or end of token) throws `invalid escape in pointer token: ~2`.
- `formatPointer` — exact inverse, escaping `~` → `~0` before `/` → `~1`.
- `resolveTokens` — the shared walker. Arrays require `0` or a leading-zero-free digit string and an in-range index; objects require an own property (via `hasOwnProperty.call`, so `/toString` fails and `/__proto__` works); scalars throw `cannot index into <type>`. Each message carries the pointer up to and including the failing token.
- Also exports helpers `hasOwn`, `typeName`, `isArrayIndex` for reuse.

`src/patch.js`
- `applyPatch` validates the patch is an array and the document is JSON, then works on a `deepCopy`, so inputs are never touched and a failure mid-patch leaves nothing behind. Every thrown error is re-wrapped as a `PatchError` with the operation `index`; pointer failures keep their message and carry the `PointerError` as `cause`.
- `prepare` validates shape before running: non-object operations, unknown/missing `op`, and missing `path`/`value`/`from`.
- `deepCopy` and object writes use `Object.defineProperty`, so `__proto__` becomes an ordinary own property and prototypes stay intact.
- `add` inserts into arrays (`-` appends, index may equal length), `replace` on `''` swaps the whole document, `remove` on `''` throws, `move` is a no-op for equal pointers and rejects moving into its own child, `copy` inserts an independent copy, and `test` uses a recursive `jsonEqual` (order-insensitive members, ordered elements, no coercion).

goal.objective:
`src/index.js` must export `parsePointer`, `formatPointer`, `resolve`, `applyPatch` and the error classes `PointerError` and `PatchError`; how the work is split across files under `src/` is up to you. `parsePointer(pointer)` turns pointer text into decoded reference tokens: the empty string is no tokens, and any other pointer must start with `/` and is split on every following `/`, so `'/'` is one empty token and `'//'` is two. Inside a token `~1` decodes to `/` and `~0` decodes to `~`, decoded left to right in one pass so `'/~01'` is the single token `~1`; a `~` followed by anything else throws `invalid escape in pointer token: ~2`. `formatPointer(tokens)` is the exact inverse, escaping `~` before `/`.

`resolve(document, pointer)` walks the document token by token and returns the selected value; the empty pointer returns the document itself. Inside an array a token must be `0` or a digit string with no leading zero, and it must be less than the length, otherwise `invalid array index: 01 at /list/01` or `index out of range: 3 at /list/3`. Inside an object the token must name an own property, otherwise `missing property: x at /a/x`. A token applied to a string, number, boolean or null throws `cannot index into string at /name/0`. Each of these carries the pointer up to and including the failing token, and every one is a `PointerError`.

`applyPatch(document, operations)` returns a new document with every operation applied. It never modifies its arguments and never shares structure with them: the document and every inserted value are deep-copied, so an empty patch still returns an independent copy. If any operation fails, the call throws and the document is left exactly as it was. The operations are `add`, `remove`, `replace`, `move`, `copy` and `test`. `add` creates or overwrites an object member, and inside an array it inserts before the given index, where the index may equal the length and the token `-` appends. `remove` and `replace` require an existing target, and `replace` on the empty pointer replaces the whole document while `remove` on it throws `cannot remove the whole document`. `move` removes the value at `from` and adds it at `path`, is a no-op when the two pointers are equal, and throws `cannot move a value into its own child` when `from` is a proper prefix of `path`. `copy` adds an independent copy of the value at `from`. `test` compares the value at `path` with `value` as JSON — object members in any order, array elements in order, and no type coercion — and throws `test failed at /a/y` when they differ.

Every failure from `applyPatch` is a `PatchError` whose `index` is the 0-based position of the operation that failed; when the cause was a pointer failure, the message is that failure's message and `cause` is the `PointerError`. Operations are checked before they run: a non-object operation throws `operation must be an object`, an unrecognised or missing `op` throws `unknown operation: frob`, and missing members throw `add requires a path`, `add requires a value` or `move requires a from`. A patch that is not an array throws `patch must be an array`, and data that is not JSON throws `document is not JSON data` or `value is not JSON data`. Keys that shadow `Object.prototype`, including `__proto__`, are ordinary own properties throughout: adding `/__proto__` must leave the result's prototype and every other object alone, and resolving `/toString` on an empty object must fail. Change only files under src/. Do not modify anything under test/ or package.json, and add no dependencies: node_modules must not exist. The standard is `node --test test/*.test.js` passing in the workspace root.
